report_name: Researchers Uncover New Surveillance Backdoors in Chinese-Made Routers

threat_actors.name: Unidentified ZBT Backdoor Actor
threat_actors.description: An unidentified actor responsible for embedding the Darklantern and Speakingstone backdoors into the firmware of Zbtlink routers, likely for state-sponsored surveillance and network traffic redirection.

attack_patterns.name: System Firmware
attack_patterns.description: The Darklantern and Speakingstone backdoors are embedded within the router's firmware, ensuring they persist across reboots and factory resets.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: The router's firmware firewall is intentionally configured to allow inbound internet traffic to the backdoor's listening port (UDP/38686).

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: The Darklantern and Speakingstone backdoors provide a covert remote access channel for an attacker to gain privileged access to the device.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Local System
attack_patterns.description: Once connected to the backdoor, an attacker can access information on the router and monitor traffic on the local network it manages.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
attack_patterns.description: The backdoors are embedded into the router hardware's firmware by the manufacturer before being sold globally under various brand names, indicating a supply chain compromise.

malware.name: Darklantern
malware.description: A backdoor found in Zbtlink routers that functions as a passive listener, opening UDP port 38686 to await incoming connections from an attacker. It is considered an earlier version of the Endlessdoors implant.

malware.name: Speakingstone
malware.description: A surveillance implant and backdoor found in Zbtlink routers, considered to be another variant and an earlier iteration of the Endlessdoors implant.

malware.name: EndlessDoors
malware.description: A previously discovered backdoor in ZBT routers, of which Darklantern and Speakingstone are considered to be earlier versions.

identities.name: Shenzhen Zhibotong Electronics Co. (ZBT)
identities.description: The Chinese manufacturer of the routers found to contain the Darklantern and Speakingstone backdoors in their firmware.

identities.name: Zbtlink
identities.description: A brand name under which routers manufactured by ZBT containing surveillance backdoors are sold.

identities.name: DeepOrange
identities.description: A white-label brand name under which a ZBT router with the newly discovered backdoors was sold.

infrastructure.name: Darklantern Backdoor Listener
infrastructure.description: A passive listener on UDP port 38686 embedded in Zbtlink routers, which allows attackers to establish a remote connection.

indicators.name: Darklantern Backdoor Inbound Connection
indicators.pattern:
title: Darklantern Backdoor Inbound Connection
id: 2b9c1a8e-5f6d-4b3a-8c1d-9e0f1a2b3c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects unsolicited inbound UDP traffic to port 38686, which is used by the Darklantern backdoor found in Zbtlink routers.
references:
  - https://www.darkreading.com/vulnerabilities-threats/chinese-routers-sold-worldwide-backdoors
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-28
tags:
  - attack.t1219
level: high
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    dst_port: 38686
    protocol: udp
    action: 'allow'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects network traffic consistent with the Darklantern backdoor, which listens for inbound connections on UDP port 38686. The router's firewall is configured to allow this traffic.
